items.title: Angus Taylor promises permanent tax cuts and to reinstate all negative gearing
items.description: The Coalition would repeal all of Labor's negative gearing and capital gains changes and spend $22.5 billion over four years handing back tax "bracket creep" to workers if elected.

items.title: The budget reply is a reminder times have changed and attention is short
items.description: To appreciate how much times have changed, it is worth comparing the opposition leader's budget reply speech to Peter Dutton's.

items.title: Why millennials and gen Z feel ripped off by this budget
items.description: The prime minister said this budget was about fixing intergenerational inequality, but online, gen Z and the millennials are hearing a different narrative.

items.title: Live: Trump enters Xi's inner sanctum as Beijing visit turns personal
items.description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are set for another day of ceremony and diplomacy after a major meeting between the pair yesterday. Follow live.

items.title: Israeli nationalists mark annexation of East Jerusalem
items.description: Thousands of Israeli nationalists, including young boys, join crowds chanting death threats towards Palestinians while marching through Jerusalem Old City.

items.title: Delta Goodrem reaches Eurovision grand final after fiery performance
items.description: Delta Goodrem has performed her pop ballad Eclipse at Eurovision in Vienna, the 11th time Australia has appeared in the musical extravaganza.

items.title: Breaking: Australia records first reported death from diphtheria in almost a decade
items.description: The Northern Territory has recorded the country's first reported death from diphtheria in almost a decade, as experts urge people to get vaccinated.

items.title: Live: ASX opens higher as Wall Street rallies with records
items.description: The ASX opens higher in morning trading after rallies on Wall Street. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Live: US vote to halt Iran war narrowly defeated
items.description: Israel and Lebanon have reported a productive first day of talks in Washington as the deadline for the ceasefire between the two countries approaches. Follow live.

items.title: Hospitalisation of young babies almost halved by new immunisation program
items.description: A new immunisation program for pregnant mothers and newborns has almost halved the number of young babies being hospitalised with a serious respiratory virus, according to a new report.

items.title: Surfers conquer 'terrifying' tidal rapid in remote WA
items.description: Pro surfers Anthony Walsh and Dylan Graves have conquered the never-before-surfed Talbot Bay tidal rapid in Western Australia's remote north.

items.title: Soon after John quit the Liberal Party, the strange phone calls started
items.description: When John Ternel quit the Victorian Liberal Party this week the party mistakenly sent an email to members saying he had died. Mr Ternel says the ordeal confirmed to him that the Victorian Liberals are in shambles.

items.title: Breaking: Matthew Wale becomes Solomon Islands prime minister after secret ballot win
items.description: Matthew Wale is the new prime minister of Solomon Islands after winning a vote in the Pacific island nation's parliament.

items.title: Archaeologists restoring oldest colonial-era boat ever found in Australia
items.description: Maritime archaeologists are working to restore the oldest colonial-era boat ever found in Australia, discovered during the construction of the Barangaroo metro station in 2018.

items.title: Melanie Lynskey joins the fight for justice after NZ's Pike River Mine disaster
items.description: Standing side by side with real-life heroes Anna Osborne and Sonya Rockhouse, the Yellow Jackets star is a passionate ally for their cause.

items.title: It's been 20 years since the wrong Guy was interviewed by the BBC
items.description: Guy Gomo reflects on his infamous live TV mix-up, which has been immortalised as one of the greatest TV blunders of all time.

items.title: ABC news quiz: A Eurovision boycott, a pungent frog and a mysterious red globule
items.description: This is not the week to boycott the news quiz, when a particularly ripe frog and a big, red … something … await you.

items.title: Chinese Australians say Coalition pitch to cut non-citizens' welfare 'sounds like One Nation'
items.description: Chinese Australians have lashed the Coalition's plan to block non-citizens from accessing welfare services, likening the opposition's targeting of migrants to One Nation.

items.title: Trust tax could hurt young, not just ultra-wealthy, tax advisors warn
items.description: The federal budget includes a new 30 per cent minimum tax on discretionary trusts. Experts say it is not just the ultra-wealthy that will be hit.

items.title: National commissioner says review into Kumanjayi Little Baby won't 'cut it'
items.description: The National Commissioner for Indigenous children has criticised the selection of a retired NSW police commissioner and long-standing NT public servant as the leaders of a review into the territory's child protection system.

items.title: Overdose at Crown Melbourne every two weeks, data shows
items.description: Paramedics have attended more than 50 suspected overdoses at Crown Melbourne in the past two years, data released exclusively to the ABC shows.

items.title: Abandoned base's toxic waste clean-up deadline rejected
items.description: The Australian government has officially ruled out cleaning up Antarctica's contaminated Wilkes Station before the end of the decade, as previously recommended by a federal parliamentary committee.

items.title: Ten still in hospital after bus rollover in north Queensland
items.description: Queensland police have described a "confronting scene" at a bus crash on a remote stretch of the Bruce Highway on Thursday afternoon.

items.title: Indigenous housing collapse puts families at risk of homelessness
items.description: Tenants in some Mount Isa homes have endured years without repairs, hot water or proper leases and now one corporation's failures could leave them homeless.

items.title: Community decries government 'arrogance' over fracking bill
items.description: Producers on South Australia's Limestone Coast say they are stunned by a government proposal to lift the fracking ban in the region.
